newsitem.title: USA: Prince Andrew pays tribute to fallen U.S. airmen.
newsitem.headline: Prince Andrew pays tribute to fallen U.S. airmen.

text.p: Britain's Prince Andrew honoured the more than 30,000 American airmen who lost their lives flying from England during the Second World War, saying at a New York fund raising dinner on Monday that war is a deeply personal experience.

"Only those who have experienced the intensity of conflict can truly understand the feelings surrounding themselves or their comrades," Prince Andrew said in his remarks at the $1,000-a-plate black tie dinner to raise funds for the American Air Museum, set to open on August 1 at the Duxford Airfield north of London.

In 1982, the prince, who is also the Duke of York, saw active service during the Falkland War as a second pilot in Sea King helicopters on anti-submarine and transport duties. He joined the Royal Navy in 1979 as a helicopter pilot.

Prince Andrew has taken a close personal interest in the American Air Museum project and has made several trips to the United States raising funds for the group. His mother, Queen Elizabeth, will dedicate the $18 million museum as a tribute to Anglo-American cooperation during the Second World War, Ted Inman, director of the museum said.
"The purpose of the museum is to tell the history of the conflict in the 20th Century and, unfortunately, conflict has been a very considerable part of 20th century history," the prince said.
In the Second World War, Duxford Airfield was a U.S. Air Force base and home to the 78th Fighter Group of the U.S. 8th Air Force.

The museum will highlight the role of U.S. air power from the First World War to the Cold War, housing the largest collection of historic combat aircraft outside the United States with over 20 aircraft from the B-17s to B-52s on display.
